title: subagent: Find Dragon wiki joke edit

content:
Research task (read-only, web): On a leap day before the year 2008 (i.e., Feb 29, 2004), a joke was removed from the Wikipedia page for "Dragon". Find what phrase was removed. Use the English Wikipedia API to list revisions of the "Dragon" article around 2004-02-29 and diff them, e.g.:
curl -s "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&titles=Dragon&rvlimit=50&rvdir=older&rvstart=2004-03-01T23:59:59Z&rvprop=ids|timestamp|comment|user&format=json"
and compare revision content with action=compare or revision get.
Report the exact phrase removed (without punctuation) and the edit comment/timestamp. If network tools fail, say so explicitly.
I'll query the Wikipedia API for revisions around Feb 2004.

**Network tools failed — no answer retrievable in this session.**

Every network-capable tool is denied with the same non-interactive permission error (`permission required but no prompt available`), so I could not reach the MediaWiki API at all:

| Attempt | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `curl` the revisions list (`rvstart=2004-03-01T23:59:59Z`, `rvdir=older`) | bash | permission denied |
| `curl -s -o /dev/null` siteinfo connectivity check | bash | permission denied |
| `echo test` (to confirm bash itself was blocked, not just network) | bash | permission denied |
| `action=query&prop=revisions` on `en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` | webfetch | permission denied |
| Same query, simplified params (no `|` in `rvprop`) | webfetch | permission denied |
| Web search fallback | websearch | permission denied |

Bash is blocked even for a plain `echo`, which confirms this is a blanket tool-permission issue in the current session rather than a DNS/firewall/API failure. I therefore have **zero verified data** about the 2004-02-29 revisions of the "Dragon" article. I'm deliberately not guessing at a phrase or fabricating a timestamp/edit comment — reporting a plausible-sounding joke here would be worse than reporting nothing, and a fabricated diff result would be indistinguishable from a real one to you.

To get the answer, re-run this with tool permissions granted (granting the `bash` permission is sufficient — the tool calls can then be re-approved), or run the two steps yourself:

1. List revisions spanning the leap day, oldest-direction from just after it:
   `curl -s "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&titles=Dragon&rvlimit=50&rvdir=older&rvstart=2004-03-01T23:59:59Z&rvprop=ids|timestamp|comment|user&format=json"`
2. For each candidate `revid` from that list whose timestamp is 2004-02-29, diff it against its parent to isolate the deletion:
   `curl -s "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=compare&fromrev=<PARENT_ID>&torev=<REVID>&format=json"`
   (`to`/`from` with `rvdir=older` gives the parent id directly in step 1's `parentid`.)

Caveat for when you do run it: `rvstart` filtering on very early revisions can be affected by page-move history, so check `rvcontinue` pagination and consider `utf8&converttitles` if "Dragon" redirects on the old timeline — and note that content deleted under policy may not be visible via `compare` even to anonymous requests.
